```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest) 
library(multcomp) 

#flatten data
df_clean_numeric <- df_with_clusters %>%
  mutate(across(
    c(Quant, Sigma, Connect, Tau1, Tau2, NPQ, qP, ABQ, qm, nTau1, nTau2, nCon, Fm, Fo), 
    ~ map_dbl(.x, ~ mean(as.numeric(unlist(.x)), na.rm = TRUE))
  ))
#################################################################
###WITHIN PHENOTYPES, are there differences across wavelengths?##
#################################################################
# 2. Convert wavelength (col) to a factor so R treats them as distinct categories
df_clean_numeric$col <- as.factor(df_clean_numeric$col)

# 1. Filter down to just Phenotype 1
pheno1_data <- df_clean_numeric %>% filter(K_3 == 1)

# 3. Fit the mixed model (matching their script's logic)
# 'col' is the wavelength, 'SampleID_clean' is the individual coral random effect, 
# and 'stage' is the timepoint random effect.
fit_quant_p1 <- lmer(Sigma ~ col + (1 | SampleID_clean) + (1 | stage), 
                     data = pheno1_data, REML = FALSE)

# Check the main effect ANOVA table
anova(fit_quant_p1)

# 4. Run the pairwise Tukey post-hoc tests on wavelength
tukey_res <- glht(fit_quant_p1, linfct = mcp(col = "Tukey"))

# 5. Get the Bonferroni-adjusted p-values
summary(tukey_res, test = adjusted("bonferroni"))
```

```{r}
#this is using manova but thats not what paper did

# 1. Select your 9 primary metrics and bundle them into a matrix
metrics_matrix <- as.matrix(df_clean_numeric[, c("Quant", "Sigma", "Connect", "Tau1", "Tau2", "NPQ", "qP", "ABQ", "qm")])

# 2. Fit the multivariate model against your Phenotypes (Cluster)
manova_fit <- manova(metrics_matrix ~ K_3, data = df_clean_numeric)

# 3. View the global test results using Pillai's Trace (the most robust metric)
summary(manova_fit, test = "Pillai")

summary.aov(manova_fit)



#LDA
library(MASS)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Fit the LDA using your 9 metrics to predict the Cluster
lda_fit <- lda(K_3 ~ Quant + Sigma + Connect + Tau1 + Tau2 + NPQ + qP + ABQ + qm, 
               data = df_clean_numeric)

# 2. Project your data into the new LDA space
lda_data <- as.data.frame(predict(lda_fit)$x)
lda_data$Cluster <- df_clean_numeric$Cluster

# 3. Plot the phenotypes in the multi-metric space
ggplot(lda_data, aes(x = LD1, y = LD2, color = Cluster)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Phenotype Separation Driven by All 9 Metrics",
       x = "Discriminant Linear Axis 1",
       y = "Discriminant Linear Axis 2")
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(lme4) 

# Ensure variables are factors and drop rows missing ED50 or site data
df_modeling <- annot_master %>%
  mutate(across(c(starts_with("K_"), site), as.factor)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(ED50), !is.na(site))

k_cols <- paste0("K_", 2:15)

# Loop through and compute AIC using lmer()
aic_mixed_all <- map_df(k_cols, function(k_name) {
  
  # Fit Mixed Model: ED50 ~ Cluster fixed effect + Site/Run random effect
  # REML = FALSE is CRITICAL here because we are comparing models with different fixed effects
  model <- lmer(as.formula(paste("ED50 ~", k_name, "+ (1 | site)")), 
                data = df_modeling, 
                REML = FALSE)
  
  data.frame(
    Model = k_name,
    AIC = AIC(model)
  )
})

# Arrange from lowest AIC (best) to highest
aic_mixed_all <- aic_mixed_all %>% arrange(AIC)
print("--- Full Dataset Mixed Model Comparisons ---")
print(aic_mixed_all)

k12_m <- lmer(ED50 ~ K_12 + (1 | site), data = df_modeling, REML = FALSE)
k13_m <- lmer(ED50 ~ K_13 + (1 | site), data = df_modeling, REML = FALSE)
k2_m  <- lmer(ED50 ~ K_2 + (1 | site),  data = df_modeling, REML = FALSE)

# 2. Run the comparative ANOVA (Likelihood Ratio Test)
anova(k2_m, k12_m, k13_m)
#summary
summary(k12_m)
r2(k12_m)
summary(k2_m)

# 2. Extract Nakagawa's R2 values
print("--- K_12 Mixed Model R2 Breakdown ---")


print("--- K_2 Mixed Model R2 Breakdown ---")
r2(k2_m)



library(emmeans)

# 1. Calculate the estimated marginal means for each cluster group
k12_means <- emmeans(k12_m, specs = ~ K_12)

# 2. Run the pairwise post-hoc comparisons with Tukey adjustment
k12_posthoc <- pairs(k12_means, adjust = "tukey")

# 3. View the results
# (Optional: filter for only statistically significant differences)
k12_posthoc_df <- as.data.frame(k12_posthoc)

significant_differences <- k12_posthoc_df %>% 
  filter(p.value < 0.05)

print(significant_differences)
plot(k12_means, comparisons = TRUE)
```
```{r}
#using site as random effect (bc variance was so low last time)

# Keep site and clusters as regular factor variables
df_modeling <- annot_master %>%
  mutate(across(c(starts_with("K_"), site), as.factor)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(ED50), !is.na(site))

k_cols <- paste0("K_", 2:15)

# Loop using standard linear models with site as a fixed covariate
aic_fixed_covariate <- map_df(k_cols, function(k_name) {
  
  # Formula: ED50 ~ Cluster + Site (Fixed Effect)
  model <- lm(as.formula(paste("ED50 ~", k_name, "+ site")), data = df_modeling)
  
  data.frame(
    Model = k_name,
    AIC = AIC(model),
    R_squared = summary(model)$r.squared
  )
})

# Arrange from lowest AIC (best) to highest
aic_fixed_covariate <- aic_fixed_covariate %>% arrange(AIC)
print("--- Fixed Effect (Site as Covariate) Model Comparisons ---")
print(aic_fixed_covariate)


k12 <- lm(ED50 ~ K_12 + site, data = df_modeling)
k13 <- lm(ED50 ~ K_13 + site, data = df_modeling)
k2 <- lm(ED50 ~ K_2 + site, data = df_modeling)
# 2. Now run the ANOVA on that model object!
anova(k12, k13,k2)

# 1. Calculate the estimated marginal means for each cluster group
k12_means <- emmeans(k12, specs = ~ K_12)

# 2. Run the pairwise post-hoc comparisons with Tukey adjustment
k12_posthoc <- pairs(k12_means, adjust = "tukey")

# 3. View the results
# (Optional: filter for only statistically significant differences)
k12_posthoc_df <- as.data.frame(k12_posthoc)

significant_differences <- k12_posthoc_df %>% 
  filter(p.value < 0.05)

print(significant_differences)
plot(k12_means, comparisons = TRUE)
```
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(lme4) # Using standard lmer here

# 1. Filter dataset for just IRCA and clean factors
df_irca <- annot_master %>%
  filter((species) == "icra") %>%
  mutate(across(c(starts_with("K_"), site), as.factor)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(ED50), !is.na(site))

k_cols <- paste0("K_", 2:15)

# 2. Run the loop with regular lmer
aic_irca_lmer <- map_df(k_cols, function(k_name) {
  
  if(length(unique(df_irca[[k_name]])) > 1) {
    
    # Regular lmer instead of blmer
    model <- lmer(as.formula(paste("ED50 ~", k_name, "+ (1 | site)")), 
                   data = df_irca, 
                   REML = FALSE)
    
    data.frame(
      Model = k_name,
      AIC = AIC(model)
    )
  } else {
    NULL 
  }
})

print(aic_irca_lmer)

k2_i <- lmer(ED50 ~ K_2 + (1 | site), data = df_irca, REML = FALSE)
k3_i <- lmer(ED50 ~ K_3 + (1 | site), data = df_irca, REML = FALSE)
k4_i  <- lmer(ED50 ~ K_4 + (1 | site),  data = df_irca, REML = FALSE)

# 2. Run the comparative ANOVA (Likelihood Ratio Test)
anova(k2_i, k3_i, k4_i)



library(emmeans)

# 1. Calculate the estimated marginal means for each cluster group
k2_i_means <- emmeans(k2_i, specs = ~ K_2)

# 1. Run the pairwise contrasts
k2_i_posthoc <- pairs(k2_i_means, adjust = "tukey")

# 2. CONVERT TO DATA FRAME FIRST so you can use filter()
k2_i_posthoc_df <- as.data.frame(k2_i_posthoc)

significant_differences <- k2_i_posthoc_df %>% 
  filter(p.value < 0.05)

print(significant_differences)
plot(k2_i_means, comparisons = TRUE)
```


```{r}
# Install blme if you don't have it: install.packages("blme")
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(blme) # <-- Bayesian mixed models to prevent singular fits

# 1. Filter dataset for just IRCA and clean factors
df_irca <- annot_master %>%
  filter(tolower(species) == "irca") %>%
  mutate(across(c(starts_with("K_"), site), as.factor)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(ED50), !is.na(site))

k_cols <- paste0("K_", 2:15)

# 2. Run the loop
aic_irca_mixed <- map_df(k_cols, function(k_name) {
  
  # Check if the cluster varies within IRCA
  if(length(unique(df_irca[[k_name]])) > 1) {
    
    # blmer keeps site as a random effect but stabilizes the math
    model <- blmer(as.formula(paste("ED50 ~", k_name, "+ (1 | site)")), 
                   data = df_irca, 
                   REML = FALSE)
    
    data.frame(
      Model = k_name,
      AIC = AIC(model)
    )
  } else {
    NULL # Skip if the cluster doesn't split up the IRCA samples
  }
})

# 3. View the results sorted by best fit
aic_irca_mixed <- aic_irca_mixed %>% arrange(AIC)
print("--- IRCA Only Random Effect Model Comparisons ---")
print(aic_irca_mixed)

```
